newsitem.title: SPAIN: INSTANT VIEW - Spain May jobless data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Spain May jobless data.

text.p: The Spanish Labour Ministry said on Monday that the unemployment rate fell to 13.26 percent in May, down from 13.61 percent in April and from 14.36 percent a year earlier. The number of jobless fell by 57,866 to 2.12 million people.
Following are analysts' comments on the data.
FRANCESCO GIORDANO, ECONOMIST AT CREDIT SUISSE

"These data are very positive. First if the downtrend in unemployment goes on, and goes on so quickly, Spain will soon stop having higher unemployment than other European countries. In particular taking into account the INE data, the unemployment spread over France is no more than 0.5 percent.

Secondly this is more evidence that the economy is picking up. All the indicators show it. This is good for the economy but it suggests a cautious approach for the Bank of Spain... a period of unchanged key rates is approaching."
WILLIAM THORNHILL, SENIOR ECONOMIST AT TECHNICAL DATA

"The number is better than the consensus predicted although ...it wasn't a complete surprise. The pace of declines has accelerated down from 14.1 percent in January. The labour reform was only legislated mid-May. The decline has much more to do with economic revival and seasonal factors. Nevertheless the decline so far this year suggests the government estimates of 200,000 (jobs to be created this year) will be exceeded. We're going for 250,000.
CARMEN HERNANSANZ, ECONOMIST AT MERRILL LYNCH

"The number is in line with what we expected. It's positive and seems that we are beginning to notice the subject of the labour reform. It has no inflation incidence. Perhaps, in this respect, the greatest repercussion is the fact that salaries this year and last are rising above inflation. This isn't going to have an impact on the markets because they are very focused on the Ecofin meeting in Luxembourg, the summit in the Netherlands and on domestic inflation."
MARIA VICTORIA NUNEZ, JUNIOR ECONOMIST SOCIETE GENERALE
"We typically have falls of 50,000 or 60,000 in May. Good weather arrives and then there are unemployment declines as services pick up. The labour reform is also helping."
"The number is pretty good. The labour reform should continue to produce declines.

"The fall in unemployment of almost 60,000 in May was in line with the estimate given last week and with our own estimates and one sees that employment is going to have a fairly good year this year as is private consumption."
"It's true that the governor of the Bank of Spain, Luis Angel Rojo, was worried about the rise in salaries but the public-sector salary freeze will moderate the upside pressures."

"The May unemployment number is positive. It seems that macroeconomic policy is bearing fruit. But we have to wait for further data to see whether this progress is sustainable. There is an effect from labour reform that is cutting costs and reducing uncertainty, particularly the latter. The number itself won't affect the markets because they are focused on EMU themes and the Ecofin meeting."
